sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Russell Brand's Rape and Sexual Assault Trial Begins
cards.content: Russell Brand's trial for rape and sexual assault started with the prosecution describing him as "ruthless" and a "sexual predator". Six women accuse him of various offenses between 1999 and 2009 including rape sexual assault and indecent assault. The prosecutor says Brand's behavior was "indiscriminate and voracious" and that he would "appear indifferent" after the incidents. The jury heard details of the alleged offenses including incidents where Brand allegedly raped and assaulted several women.

cards.title: Ukrainian man on trial in Germany for Nord Stream pipeline sabotage
cards.content: A Ukrainian man named Serhii Kuznetsov has gone on trial in Hamburg Germany accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines four years ago. The prosecution says Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs and is charged with a war crime. His defence team claims there is no concrete evidence against him and that he cannot have a fair trial because he is a soldier who is bound to secrecy. The case is sensitive in Germany which is one of Ukraine's closest allies.

cards.title: Australian Navy Ship Finds Hidden Video Device in Female-Only Space
cards.content: An Australian navy ship HMAS Leeuwin had a hidden video recording device found in one of its cabins. The discovery was confirmed by the Australian Defence Force and was reportedly made in a female-only space. The incident has raised concerns that the device may have captured private moments of female sailors without their knowledge or consent and that footage may have been uploaded online. The Defence Force has launched an investigation and is providing support to affected crew members but has not yet revealed more details about the discovery or the investigation.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Tech Firms Unveil AI-Powered Devices for Holiday Season
cards.content: Tech companies like Apple Amazon and Microsoft are introducing new devices with artificial intelligence or AI capabilities hoping to sell them to consumers during the holiday season. These devices such as smart home hubs and tablets claim to make AI more personal and accessible. While some analysts are skeptical about how well these devices will sell others believe that getting affluent early adopters on board now could be a win.

cards.title: ASML Reports Strong Profits, Boosts Stock with Future Tool Demand
cards.content: ASML a company that makes tools for making semiconductors reported strong profits and said some customers are interested in buying its tools for future years. This has made investors feel better about the company's future demand. The CEO said customers are increasing their orders because they think AI-related investments will keep growing. ASML's CEO also said the company will need to increase its production to meet demand and is looking at ways to do that. The company's stock has gone up a lot this year and it's expected to keep growing.

cards.title: Anthropic Asks Court to Reconsider Pentagon Blacklisting Appeal
cards.content: Anthropic an American AI company is asking a federal court to reconsider its appeal in a case against the Pentagon. The Pentagon's Secretary of War blacklisted Anthropic's AI models in March because the company wouldn't allow its technology to be used for mass surveillance or lethal autonomous warfare. Anthropic sued the Trump administration to undo the action but the court upheld the blacklisting in September. Now Anthropic is arguing that the court ignored evidence that the blacklisting was retaliation for the company's speech about AI safety.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Weightlifter's BPC-157 Use Ends in Fatigue, Anxiety After Just Three Days
cards.place: The single best geographic location to associate with this story is:
cards.content: Dylan Meetze a weightlifter stopped taking BPC-157 a peptide drug after feeling horrible and experiencing fatigue anxiety twitching eyes and muscles after just three days. He bought the drug online and was one of over 1000 people who told doctors they had used it. Meetze's story is part of a growing trend of people using unapproved peptide drugs which are often promoted by online influencers and wellness enthusiasts. Despite the lack of clinical trials and evidence of potential harm the FDA is considering easing restrictions on these drugs which has sparked concerns among scientists and health experts. Meetze and others who have taken the drug are now dealing with the consequences including a lack of data and online skepticism from those who promote the drugs.

cards.title: Boy Kibble Diet Criticized for High Protein, Low Veggie Content
cards.content: Boy kibble is a simple meal plan where people eat the same food every day usually a rice base with ground meat and optional avocado. It's popular among men especially those trying to increase their fitness as it provides a reliable way to meet protein goals. However experts say the diet can be too high in protein and low in vegetables which is a concern. They suggest adding vegetables to the meals and switching up the diet occasionally to get a variety of nutrients.

cards.title: GLP-1 medication slows aging process, study finds
cards.content: Scientists have found that a type of medication called GLP-1 may slow down the aging process. This medication is typically used to help people with diabetes and weight loss. Studies have shown that it can improve the health of many parts of the body lowering the risk of certain diseases. Researchers have been studying how GLP-1 affects the aging process by looking at biomarkers or biological signs of aging. They found that the medication seemed to slow down aging in people who took it reducing their biological age by 3-6 years. The study's leader says that the effects of the medication are mostly due to weight loss and blood sugar control. Other studies have found similar results showing that GLP-1 medications may have anti-aging effects.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Zimbabwe Sets Up $500 Million Reserve for Food Security
cards.content: Zimbabwe plans to create a $500 million reserve to help with food security if a drought happens. The government thinks a big El Niño weather event could cause dry conditions and make it hard to grow food so they're getting ready by setting up this reserve.

cards.title: African Countries Urged to Focus on Carbon Removal in Specific Locations
cards.content: A new report says African countries should focus on removing carbon dioxide from the air in specific locations balancing efforts to fight climate change with their own development goals. This approach could bring in funding create jobs and support agriculture and industry but it's not a guarantee. Right now Africa's carbon removal sector is still developing with limited science infrastructure and expertise. The report highlights potential opportunities like biochar and enhanced rock weathering and points to Kenya's Rift Valley as an early hub for carbon capture. But it also warns that uncertain carbon markets lack of local standards and environmental risks could limit the benefits unless African countries strengthen their institutions and safeguards.

cards.title: Indonesia sees worst wildfires in decade with 1.06 million hotspots detected.
cards.content: Indonesia has seen a massive increase in wildfires with over 1.06 million hotspots detected as of October 14 2026. This is the worst wildfire season in a decade. Dry conditions linked to the Super El Niño event are making the fires harder to control and increasing the risk of more outbreaks. The smoke from the fires has spread to Malaysia and Singapore causing air quality problems and health concerns. The cause of the fires is linked to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices and unusually dry weather.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: La Bola Negra Sweeps Nation with Gay Drama Oscar Favourite
cards.content: A new movie called La Bola Negra is making waves in the film industry. It's a sweeping drama that tells the stories of three gay men across a century and it's currently second favourite to win the top prize at the Oscars. The film has received widespread critical acclaim and is a commercial hit in its native Spain. It's a masterpiece of storytelling with a unique blend of romance historical epic and family drama. The film's directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have brought their own experiences and perspectives to the story and the film's themes of gay desire persecution and self-punishment are handled with sensitivity and courage.

cards.title: Lena Dunham Revives Girls for Limited Run with Original Cast
cards.content: Lena Dunham the creator of the popular TV show Girls announced that the show will return for a limited run after a 10-year hiatus. The revival will feature five episodes and reunite the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. Dunham said she's been missing the characters and that they started talking to her again around her 40th birthday. The show will explore what's happened to the characters since they were in their 20s.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voices New Animated "The Baddies" Adaptation
cards.content: Welsh actor Rob Brydon is voicing a new animated adaptation of the popular children's book "The Baddies" over the Christmas period. The story follows a troll a ghost and a witch as they try to steal a blue spotty hanky from a brave little girl. Brydon will be joined by Gavin and Stacey co-stars Sheridan Smith and Alison Steadman as well as Hammed Animashaun Robyn Cara and Francesca Mills. The half-hour special celebrates kindness and standing up to bullies and features beautiful animation.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: US Inflation Surges to 3.7%, Driven by Higher Gas Prices
cards.content: US inflation rose more than expected in September reaching 3.7%. Higher gasoline prices driven by Middle East energy supply disruptions are the main cause. Inflation has been above the US Federal Reserve's 2% target which is considered stable for an economy. Experts will closely watch if energy costs affect other areas like food prices and drive inflation higher. Food inflation is currently flat but core inflation which excludes food and energy is at 2.6%.

cards.title: Bank of America Fined $1.2 Billion for Money Laundering Failures
cards.content: Bank of America has been fined $1.2 billion for failing to detect and report suspicious financial activity including money laundering and illegal transactions. The bank didn't flag transactions that might have involved Chinese money laundering networks or had connections to the US-Mexico border. This means the bank didn't take its own responsibility to detect and report suspicious activity seriously instead relying on others to do the job. As a result the US Treasury Department has imposed the third-largest fine ever and Bank of America has admitted to violating anti-money laundering rules.

cards.title: Saudi Engineer Charged with Secretly Recording OpenAI Executives
cards.content: A Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan has been charged with secretly installing a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California. Alfozan who worked as an engineer at OpenAI allegedly hid the device in a TV's USB port in an executive conference room. OpenAI discovered the device and used its AI models to track it back to Alfozan who was fired. Prosecutors say Alfozan tried to capture sensitive communications about OpenAI's AI product.
